_instructions: Copy to content/reviews/<slug>.json, delete this key, and read docs/EDITORIAL.md first. Fill runs[] from the actual session before writing any analysis. If you did not run the skill, set evidenceBasis to source-review, empty runs[], and write a basisNote — do not describe what the skill 'would' do as though you saw it.
title: Skill Name Review: the one-line angle
description: Two sentences for search results and the listing card. What it is, and the single most useful thing a reader learns here.

author.name: TrustedSkills Team
author.bio: We assess AI agent skills by installing them, running them against real work, and reading the source. We don't accept payment for reviews.

runs.task: The real job you pointed it at. Be specific — 'audited the category pages on trustedskills.dev for missing structured data', not 'tested SEO features'.
runs.outcome: What actually came back. Include what it got right, what it missed, and anything that surprised you. Past tense, indicative mood. If you find yourself writing 'would', stop — you're predicting, not reporting.
runs.environment: Anything about the setup that shaped the result — Playwright installed, MCP servers connected, OS.

summary: The quick verdict. Markdown. Three or four sentences: what it is, who it's for, and the one caveat that matters most.

strengths.title: 🎯 A specific, concrete strength
strengths.body: Why it matters, grounded in what you saw during the run. Avoid restating the README.

limitations.title: 🔒 A specific, concrete limitation
limitations.body: Where it stops, and who that hurts. Every skill has some — a review with nothing critical to say isn't a review.

bestFor.title: 👨‍💻 A reader type
bestFor.body: Why this skill fits their work specifically.

notFor: Who should skip it, and why. One short paragraph, markdown.

sections.heading: Optional extra section
sections.body: Free-form markdown, rendered after the runs and before the strengths. Use for 'what's included', comparison tables (GFM tables work), or installation notes. Delete if unused.

faq.question: A question a reader would actually type into Google.
faq.answer: A direct answer in two or three sentences. These become FAQPage structured data, so they need to be genuinely useful standalone.
